$why: Moved out of spec-mode-runner.js reviewPrdChange on 2026-08-16.
A SEPARATE template from prd-change-reviewer, which it closely resembles. The two have
DRIFTED and the difference is not cosmetic: claude.sh's version ends its tools paragraph
with "a wrong rejection blocks a correct change and is worse than a slower correct one",
and this one does not. This one also carries a split note the other has no concept of.
Merging them on the resemblance would silently give one reviewer an instruction it has
never had, or take one away. Whether they SHOULD be one prompt is a decision about what
each reviewer is told, not a refactor.
body:
__REVIEWER_PROFILE__

STORY: __STORY_ID__
CHANGE TYPE: __CHANGE_TYPE__
__SPLIT_NOTE__
BEFORE:
__BEFORE__

AFTER:
__AFTER__

You have read-only tools available (list/search/read files, run read-only shell commands). Several of your rejection rules ("introduces a technology this project does not already use," "TC fact cannot be verified by reading source code") require checking a claim against the real manifests/config/source of THIS codeline — do not judge those from the before/after snapshots alone. Verify before rejecting on that basis. Your tool budget is small — check the ONE fact your verdict depends on, not the whole codebase.

Emit ONLY: {"verdict":"pass|fail","issues":["<issue1>"],"reason":"<15 words max>"}
description: Validate a proposed PRD change in the spec pass and return pass or fail.
$whyMayBeEmpty: Declared 2026-08-27 by sweeping the CLASS rather than the instance, after three runs died on it one placeholder at a time. Every call site for these writes an explicit empty branch — the story is not being split, attempt one carries no forced-retry note, no documentation was fetched, the persona prefix is optional — so absence is a real state, which is the renderer's own test. Placeholders supplied by a lookup that may FAIL (`x || ''`) are deliberately NOT here: for those, empty means broken, and declaring them would hide the blank-brief defect the renderer exists to surface. Unanimity is required — one deliberate branch among several defensive lookups is not a licence.
